name: Encharge
description: Email that sends itself when something happens in a CRM, in billing, or in the product. Co-founded by Kalo Yankulov after an earlier tool, HeadReach, lost a Google API. Bulgaria.

whyItPrints: Glue between the billing system and the inbox. An AppSumo lifetime deal filled the early list. Search is the later channel. A later video title says he sold the business. I did not find the buyer or the terms, so this page does not name either.
whyThisMatters:
Encharge sends email when a billing event or a product event happens. It connects to the CRM and to the payment system, then runs the sequence. Kalo Yankulov started it after HeadReach, an earlier product, lost a Google API it depended on. Bulgaria.

The numbers are a pile, and they are not one business at one date. In June 2019 he had four thousand dollars of pre-orders: fifty people buying lifetime access at eighty-nine dollars, in two weeks. HeadReach, the previous product, was at two thousand a month. A YouTube recap, as Starter Story tells it, says an AppSumo lifetime deal brought in nearly a million in about a month, and that about fifty thousand was spent on a writing team and a few hundred articles. Starter Story also prints an estimate of about thirty-five thousand a month as of January 2024, from one public source. That line is an estimate. A later video title says he sold the company. I did not find who bought it or what they paid, so those stay blank.

You pay so the email goes out when the subscription changes, without someone pressing send.
